children: Guinea-Bissau saw few turn out to vote on Sunday in a referendum on a proposed new constitution that would expand the power of the presidency and shrink the size of the parliament ahead of a presidential election scheduled for December.
The West African nation is currently led by military officers who seized power in a coup last year.
Poll stations were seen to be largely empty in the capital Bissau on Sunday, according to a Reuters witness, who found few voters had turned out to cast a ballot.
Citizens told a private radio station that they did not grasp the significance of the proposed changes or were unaware the vote was scheduled.
“I didn’t vote because I didn’t even know that today was voting day. I don't even know what we are voting for,” said one resident in the capital as he sat on his doorstep.
The new constitution would allow the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and cabinet. Currently, the prime minister appoints the cabinet.
It would also slash the size of the parliament in the country of around 2.2 million people from 102 to 65 seats.
It would require presidential candidates to have resided permanently in Guinea-Bissau for the previous five years, a condition not included in the current constitution.
Provisional results of the referendum are due on September 1.
Bissau's military-led government seized power last November just a day before the electoral commission was due to announce the results of a presidential election.
